summary:
Mayotte is a French overseas department in the Indian Ocean and stands under the French national framework. The national rules on identity documents, criminal law, anti-discrimination, marriage and custody placement extend to the island, including its places of deprivation of liberty.

Formal entitlement and lived experience diverge. A teacher at the university centre of Mayotte and his Malagasy partner married at Sada town hall in 2023, after what reporting described as a long and complicated path, on a predominantly Muslim island where the written law is not the whole of what a couple faces.

Legal representation is thinly available locally. A French-language directory of LGBT-friendly lawyers returns no referenced practitioner for Mayotte's towns, including Mamoudzou, Koungou, Dzaoudzi and Sada, while listing a Paris-based lawyer admitted to the Conseil d'État and Cour de cassation, working in persons and family law, as available.
tangentialFactors:
Mayotte's legal position is an outlier in its region: it is one of the few jurisdictions in Africa and the Muslim-majority world where marriages between people of the same sex can be performed.

That position is set by the national framework rather than by any local legislative choice, and the island's predominantly Muslim social environment is where the divergence from the statute is felt.
localsOnly:
Residents who need counsel on gender identity, family or persons matters have no locally referenced LGBT-friendly practitioner in Mamoudzou, Koungou, Dzaoudzi or Sada. The directory's only listed option is a Paris-based lawyer admitted to the Conseil d'État and Cour de cassation.

A marriage between two men at Sada town hall in 2023 took a long and complicated path locally, despite the national regime that permits it.
outOfScopeNotes:
No region-specific record of trans-specific violence, hate-crime enforcement or police conduct on Mayotte was identified in the sources reviewed.

The absence of a referenced LGBT-friendly lawyer for Mayotte's towns reflects the coverage of one French-language directory and is not a measure of how many practitioners on the island would take such cases.

No source reviewed documents how the national custody-placement rule, the legal gender-change procedure or the hate-crime provisions operate in practice on Mayotte.
